speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, please describe the painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg in detail, including when it started and how it has changed. To help me assess the severity, have you had any fever, chills, or red streaks spreading from the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Necrotizing Fasciitis (Suspected).

Given your history of diabetes, Crohn's disease, and recent steroid use, this rapidly enlarging ulcer with an ant bite history is highly concerning for a severe necrotizing soft tissue infection. I need to see the wound immediately; REQUEST IMAGES: Right_Leg_Ulcer. Also, please confirm if you have a high fever or feel generally ill right now.
